data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available for this intake (auto-dispatched by the
herdr downtime worker at 2026-10-29T03:54:28Z), so each question below was
resolved from host and repository evidence; none is blocking. Each carries the
agent's **Recommended** option, which the producer may override.

- **Q1: Given that `average_gfx_activity` already measures as saturated (100 %
  from 42 W to 123 W), is a documented negative verdict an acceptable
  deliverable for this item?**
  **Recommended:** yes — record the numbers, close the path permanently, and file
  follow-ups for the fields that do discriminate.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the item was written to test the hypothesis,
  not to assume it; the file decodes correctly (264 B v3.0, cross-checked
  against hwmon power) yet its activity field does not respond to load, so the
  honest outcome is a negative verdict with evidence. Source: two 60-sample 1 s
  captures (power 44–123 W and 42–66 W, DRAM 0.7–59.5 GB/s, activity 100 on all
  120 samples), `/tmp` probe using the `kgd_pp_interface.h` v3.0 layout.
- **Q2: If a field does pass the bar, should it replace the power-derived
  `gpu:computing:bool` as the report's GPU busy measure, or be published
  alongside it?**
  **Recommended:** publish alongside; keep power-derived authoritative until its
  own calibration item justifies switching.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): `gpu:computing:bool` is referenced by the
  report (`gpu_busy.py`, `reporting.py`), the alert `GpuComputingSustained` and
  `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`; changing its meaning inside an
  investigation item would break three consumers at once. Publishing an additive
  series keeps the comparison visible, and report adoption stays a follow-up
  (same boundary recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W). Source:
  `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`.
- **Q3: Where should the probe live, and how should a passing field reach
  Prometheus — extend the deployed bash textfile sampler, or add a Python
  sampler?**
  **Recommended:** a repo `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decoder plus a one-line
  call from the existing bash sampler; no new unit.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the sampler is a documented 10 s bash loop
  writing `gpu.prom` atomically, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` embeds
  the script verbatim; a second sampler would duplicate the unit, the textfile
  directory and the docs. Decoding a 264-byte binary blob in bash is not
  testable, so the field table belongs in Python with fixture tests. Source:
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** – Evaluate amd-smi as the GPU utilisation source for the usage report (record the decision) (completed)
- **LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4** – Proxy usage report: hardware power-based GPU busy time (15s sampling) (completed)
- **LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ** – Use the non-GPU (log-derived) local busy time as the decision-facing utilisation figure (open)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+480 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+480 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+479 more)

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the contention queue to be a bounded straggler net
(30 s, depth 2) instead of a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops
competing with real local work, while a slot that frees within seconds is
still usable.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC2 (single-source budget) and
AC4 (tests/validation).

## Change

```yaml
contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
```

Evidence (proxy.log*, 2026-10-22 19:00→22:18, 3.3 h at 60 s / depth 8): 180
queue events — 38 wins (21 %) / 142 losses (79 %), every loss at the full
60 s, 8 705 s aggregate dead wait; wins retained by budget: 20 s → 24 %,
30 s → 34 %, 45 s → 60 %. Trigger, flip criteria and the two-line rollback
live on the parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, flip criteria and rollback.
2. `proxy/config.yaml` ships 30 s / depth 2 and the surrounding comment block
   (~lines 1740-1800) records the new evidence, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline
   requirement, the 7-day observation window, the three flip criteria and the
   two-line rollback (revert to 60 / 8, restart the proxy).
3. **AC2 — single-source budget.** The shortened budget reaches the admission
   guard and the reservation endpoint through one resolver
   (`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds`); no second constant, no per-call
   default. Tests assert `wait_budget_seconds(merged config, "medium") ==
   30.0`, the guard's refusal payload and `X-Local-Admission-Budget` header
   report 30 s, `POST /llama/local/reserve` prices against the same 30 s, and
   `high` priority still resolves to 0 s — all through
   `_get_contention_queue_config`.
4. depth 2 is accepted unchanged; clamping happens only outside [1, 16]
   (values 1 and 16 pass through unchanged).
5. **AC4 — tests / validation.** Unit tests cover the swept values end to end:
   resolver 30 s, depth 2, 30 s timeout. A third waiter with 2 parked falls
   back immediately without enqueueing, and a parked waiter that is not
   served falls back at 30 s (tiny/mocked caps — never a real 30 s sleep).
6. Stale fixtures/tests that assert the shipped 60 s / 8 defaults are updated
   (`proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py::test_{cheap,fast}_config_declares_queue_policy`
   and any other shipped-config assertions), not left stale. The code-level
   defaults for a missing key stay as the inert no-config fallback and are
   documented as such (absent queue key ⇒ policy `fallback` ⇒ nothing queues).
7. Code comments in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (module docstring still says
   60 s), `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` and `proxy/proxy/router.py`
   state the single-budget contract; no behavioural change beyond the two
   config values.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated ⇒
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget.
- Out of scope: queue removal, slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model,
  client reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- The config change requires a proxy restart; deployment happens in the
  observation child after a quiet-window restart, not in this item's session.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the report/baseline child: the ≥24 h 60 s / depth 8 baseline must
  be recorded before this sweep is applied.

## Problem

The automated code-quality review (epic LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8, tag `Refactor`) filed three work items — one CRITICAL, one HIGH, one MEDIUM — against `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`, a **gitignored, untracked** local analysis scratch script:

- LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (critical, F401 unused `sys`)
- LP-0MVTJXC1D003NS8F (high, E401 multiple imports on one line)
- LP-0MVTJXCCL008DOEO (medium, I001 unsorted import block)

`.worklog/` is excluded by `.gitignore` (rule `.worklog/`, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`), and `ruff` itself honours `.gitignore` on directory recursion. Findings on untracked scratch files cannot be remediated by a commit, so each becomes a verification-only no-op item — scheduling noise, and a CRITICAL-tagged one competes with real defects in `wl next`.

## Root cause

The review scan enumerates files by explicit path (or walks the tree without honouring `.gitignore`), so gitignored paths enter the lint scope.

## Proposed fix

- Scope the scan to git-tracked files (`git ls-files`), or add explicit exclusions for gitignored paths / `.worklog/`.
- Optionally suppress findings whose file is untracked (no committable remediation path exists).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The code-quality review emits no findings for files excluded by `.gitignore` (verified by a scan covering `.worklog/analysis/` and observing no findings for it).
- [ ] A regression check covers the scan scope (test or documented scope assertion).
- [ ] No severity inflation: a finding on a gitignored path is either not filed, or filed at `low` with an explicit "untracked scratch file" note.

## Provenance

Discovered while implementing LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (no-op verification close of the F401 finding for the same gitignored file).

Make `remote-ok` the default and retire `prefer-local` with the same loud `400` (parent AC14, AC17, AC18, AC19, AC21, AC9). The default flip and the `prefer-local` retirement must land **together**: retiring the current default first would break every headerless caller, and flipping the default first would leave a silent reinterpretation path.

## Goal

One written, observable vocabulary policy: exactly two live values, `remote-ok` as the default, and a headerless client that never waits for a slot it did not ask for.

## Scope

- `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`; `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)`.
- `prefer-local` rejected through the retirement mechanism from the earlier child, with a `detail` naming both live values - never silently resolved to the new default (an explicit `prefer-local` asked to *wait*; the default does not).
- Exactly one startup log line naming the active default and the retired values; routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key.
- Test sweep: every module relying on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly, including `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` (drop `LOCAL_ONLY`) and the absent-header parameter lists; the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default.
- Document the expected behaviour shift (no queue wait by default; opportunistic local serving) so the daily usage report's local/remote split is not later read as a local-serving regression. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (two live values, parent AC21).** `VALID_PREFERENCES` is exactly the two-value tuple, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE == remote-ok`, and an absent header resolves to `remote-ok` and inherits the keep-local/no-queue behaviour. **Restates parent AC21:** `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`, so an **absent header** and any genuinely unknown value resolve to `remote-ok` and inherit AC15 + AC20. `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)` — exactly two live values. The knock-on surface is stated for the reader, because it is now the *default* path rather than a niche value: the prefill-ETA admission guard still runs (it decides whether local can serve now) but its **refusal** outcome is unreachable for this preference, and the contention queue, the deferral/retry surface and `POST /llama/local/reserve` are reachable only for `local-preferred` clients.
- **AC2 (prefer-local retired loudly, parent AC14).** An explicit `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` returns `400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`; it is never resolved to the new default; zero upstream calls. **Restates parent AC14:** `prefer-local` leaves `VALID_PREFERENCES`. An **explicit** `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` is rejected with the same stable shape as AC1 (`400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`) rather than being silently resolved to the new default. Rationale is symmetric to AC1: an explicit `prefer-local` means "wait for local when it fits the wait budget", while the new default `remote-ok` means "take local only when it is free right now" — silently reinterpreting it would deliver a materially different policy with no signal, and a client relying on the queue wait would silently start paying for remote dispatch.
- **AC3 (default observable, parent AC17).** Exactly one startup line names the active default and the retired values; a headerless request's routing line reports `preference=remote-ok` with no new log key. **Restates parent AC17:** Exactly one log line at startup (or on the first dispatch) names the active `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` and the retired values, so an operator can prove from `proxy.log` which vocabulary policy the *running* proxy applies — a deploy that ships the code without the intended config is otherwise invisible. Routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key (`preference=remote-ok` for headerless requests).
- **AC4 (test sweep, parent AC19).** Every test that depended on the implicit default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven sweep of the modules listed in the parent's existing-state section; the parent's "~55 occurrences / 16 modules" figure is stale - current grep shows 8 test modules and 69 occurrences including sources, so the sweep is grep-driven, not count-driven); `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` drops `LOCAL_ONLY`; the vocabulary tests pin both the set and the default so a silent revert fails. **Restates parent AC19:** Every test that relied on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven: the plan-time count is 8 test modules plus 2 source modules, 69 occurrences of `prefer-local` in `proxy/tests` + `proxy/proxy` outside `__pycache__`, verified 2026-10-30 — an earlier "16 modules / ~55 occurrences" figure counted a wider tree, so sweep by grep, not by count), including the pin-local parameter lists that still carry the retired spelling (`PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES = (LOCAL_ONLY, LOCAL_PREFERRED)`, `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py:592`, which must drop `LOCAL_ONLY`), and the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default so a silent revert fails.
- **AC5 (post-inversion intent matrix, parent AC9).** The matrix rows are stated in the two-value vocabulary: `local-preferred` is the only pin-local value (escalation applies to every pinned request; a remote-less chain keeps refusing), `remote-ok` asserts its two new observables rather than "unchanged", and both retired values assert `400`.
- **AC6 (shift documented, parent AC18).** `routing.md` records the two expected shifts - no queue wait by default (`contention_queue_*` lines disappear for headerless traffic) and opportunistic local serving - and the completion comment repeats them so the daily report's change is not misread as a regression. **Restates parent AC18:** The item records the two shifts: (a) **no queue wait by default** — `contention_queue_dispatch` / `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` lines disappear for headerless traffic, so the measured `queued_duration` median drops to ~0 and the remote share rises whenever the GPU is busy at request time; (b) local serving is now **opportunistic** — a headerless request is served locally only when a slot is free at that instant, so local utilisation falls and `X-Local-Route: remote` with a fall-through reason becomes the common outcome under contention. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary); the expectation is stated in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and in the completion comment so the daily proxy-usage report's shift is not mistaken for a local-serving defect.
- **AC7 (no remote-less regression, parent AC16).** The `private` model serves locally under an absent header (200, zero remote calls, no exhaustion body) - the highest-severity hazard of the inversion, asserted at the flip.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Flip `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, drop `prefer-local` from the live set and register it as retired with both successors.
2. Grep-driven sweep: set explicit headers in the affected tests, drop retired values from parameter lists.
3. Add the startup line (one emission per process) and assert it once.
4. Update the preference table, the "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`" paragraph and the metric-shift note in `routing.md` and `config.yaml`.
5. Turn the remaining contract specs green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child, the `remote-ok` semantics child (the new default must already be safe) and the `local-only` retirement child (the mechanism is shared).

# Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported saturated

Close the last 12 `saturated`-without-live-work polls by making the proxy
annotate the slot it is still draining: every abandonment records a matchable
identity (or an endpoint-wide entry), so a draining slot reads
`abandoned_busy` and only genuinely live work reports `saturated`.

## Problem statement

The AC1 fix (`LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK`) took `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` from **247 polls
(2.12 %)** to **12 polls (0.11 %)** over a comparable 11 h night, but not to
zero. Every remaining violation is a *draining* slot: llama-server has been
told to stop (the upstream stream was closed) yet has not freed the slot, and
nothing annotates it — `local_abandoned_slots=0`, so the poll reads
`saturated` even though nothing the proxy is waiting for occupies the pool.

The gap is therefore an **annotation** gap, not a liveness gap: the proxy
knows it abandoned the work, but the status builder cannot tie that
abandonment to the slot the backend is still draining.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether
  the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a draining ghost
  misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker).
  `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a ghost-driven
  `saturated` causes avoidable paid fallback.
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`.
  Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is
  as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when the pool holds only work the proxy abandoned, I
  want `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` (not `saturated`) so I can tell "busy
  because of us" from "busy because of live work".
- As the routing policy, I want a draining slot to never look saturated, so a
  needless cloud fallback is not triggered by work nobody is waiting for.
- As an analyst, I want each draining-slot abandonment attributable to a slot
  or to its endpoint, so a re-measured residual can be explained rather than
  merely counted.

## Evidence (from the AC4 run, preserved)

Re-measurement `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`, night 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30
07:00, artifacts in `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`
(`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, 12 rows, all fresh detail):

| episode | polls | attribution | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-30 06:57:36 | 3 (one second) | unattributable | `measured_cache_deficit` release 31 s earlier; `available_slots=0 total_slots=2 local_abandoned_slots=0`; pool idle again by 06:57:43 |
| 2026-10-30 06:01:20–21 | 2 | unattributable | — |
| 2026-10-29 20:19:25 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 295 s |
| 2026-10-29 20:35:03 | 1 | `prefill_deadline` | 14 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:36:23 | 2 | `no_progress_watchdog` | 182 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:47:30–31 | 2 | `prefill_deadline` | 48 s |
| 2026-10-30 01:43:11 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 520 s |

Two shapes of the same gap:

1. **Attributable (7 polls)** — an abandonment whose cancel succeeded leaves a
   slot that is still `is_processing` but carries **no** abandoned-registry
   entry (`local_abandoned_slots=0`), so the annotation does not fire.
2. **Unattributable (5 polls)** — a release with no slot identity at all
   (`measured_cache_deficit` on a record without a pinned slot), so the poll
   cannot be attributed even with the 600 s lookback.

Two further observations to confirm during implementation (not yet claimed as
causes):

- two rows (06:01:20, 01:43:11) report `available_slots=1` **alongside**
  `saturated`, which a purely-occupied pool cannot produce;
- one row reports `latency_ms=3355`, above the `/slots` detail budget, while
  `slots_detail_stale=false`.

If either turns out to be a distinct (non-lag) defect, record it as a
`discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` item rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it
   gave up on, or records an explicit "unknown slot, endpoint-wide" entry that
   the status builder can match to a processing slot on that endpoint (so a
   release without a slot id is still annotatable).
2. A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`
   until llama-server reports it free (registry TTL keeps it bounded; no
   leaked marker, no double decrement, no phantom lease).
3. `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`
   and never `idle`; a genuinely live, proxy-owned slot still reports
   `saturated` (the truthful-status contract of `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` is not
   weakened).
4. Deterministic tests (mocked `/slots` snapshot, injected clock) cover both
   shapes above, including the case where the draining slot is visible in a
   *fresh* snapshot, the endpoint-wide (unknown-slot) match, and the negative
   case (endpoint-wide entry present but the slot is owned by a live dispatch
   record → still `saturated`).
5. Re-measurement over a comparable night shows **0** `saturated`-without-live-
   work polls (baseline for this residual: 12 polls / 0.11 %, of which 5
   unattributable).
6. Full suite green through the `test` skill; docs updated where the
   abandonment → capacity interaction is described
   (`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Truthful status is not weakened** (`LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM`): an endpoint-wide
  match must never annotate a slot that a live dispatch record owns, and a
  fresh snapshot with genuinely live decode work must keep reporting
  `saturated`.
- The registry stays **in-process**, keyed by `(endpoint, slot)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s default), no
  timer task, no unbounded growth. An endpoint-wide entry needs a key that
  cannot collide with a real slot id.
- The annotation is **read-only status decoration**: it must never free or
  acquire capacity, double-decrement counters, or create a phantom lease.
- The status schema stays **additive** (`status_schema_version` 4:
  `abandoned*`, `local_abandoned_slots`, `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy`).
- **Measurement must remain possible.** `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  `_ABANDON_REASONS` currently excludes `measured_cache_deficit`, so that
  release is reported unattributable no matter how well the proxy annotates
  it — the set must be extended (with a test) or AC5 is unmeasurable.
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Existing state

- Registry: `_abandoned_slots` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), keyed
  `(endpoint_or_empty, slot_id)`; `_record_abandoned_slot` returns `None` when
  the slot id is not an `int`, so an unknown-slot abandonment is silently
  dropped — this is exactly the shape-2 gap.
- Matching: `_abandoned_slot_for(slot_id, endpoint=…)` tries the exact
  endpoint, then the legacy/default endpoint, then any endpoint carrying that
  slot id. There is no endpoint-wide (slot-less) match.
- Recording paths: `_release_unserved_dispatch` resolves the slot via
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup` *before* freeing the assignment (prefill deadline,
  client disconnect); session eviction resolves one slot per released record
  in `proxy/proxy/server.py`; the watchdog and orphan sweep record too.
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` passes **neither** slot id nor
  stream, which is the shape-2 source.
- Status builder: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` annotates `abandoned`,
  `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_at_seconds_ago`
  when the registry matches the slot id; `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0
  returns `abandoned_busy` when every generating slot is abandoned and keeps
  `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
- Residual behaviour: the 7 attributable polls reported
  `local_abandoned_slots=0` while a slot was `is_processing`, so the recorded
  identity did not match the draining slot (stale/mis-resolved id, or a slot
  the backend reassigned after the free) and the annotation never fired.
- Docs already describe the mechanism in
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (§ *Abandoned work*) and
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ *Abandoned local dispatches*).

## Desired change

1. Every abandonment path records either the slot it gave up on (resolved
   before the assignment is freed, and re-verified against the slot the
   backend actually reports) or an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry.
2. The status builder matches an endpoint-wide entry only to a processing slot
   on that endpoint that no live dispatch record owns, so the draining ghost is
   annotated and live work is not.
3. The annotation survives until llama-server reports the slot free (or the TTL
   elapses), and is dropped when the slot is observed free; re-abandoning
   refreshes it; no duplicate entries, no leak.
4. `capacity_hint` for a pool whose only work is draining stays
   `abandoned_busy` — never `saturated`, never `idle`.
5. `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` counts a `measured_cache_deficit`
   release as an abandonment event for attribution, with a test.
6. Docs updated where the abandonment → capacity interaction is described.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — abandoned-slot registry, release paths,
  endpoint-wide entry, slot re-verification.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status slot builder, endpoint-wide match,
  `compute_capacity_hint` (rule 0 unchanged in intent).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload
  (`local_abandoned_slots`).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — session-eviction slot resolution (if the recorded
  identity needs re-verification).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — registry, annotation and
  capacity-hint tests for both shapes.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — status payload contract.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — attribution set.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 7 attributable residuals are identity/matching failures,
  not TTL expiry — the longest release→poll gap observed is 520 s against a
  900 s TTL. Verify by logging the recorded slot id against the processing slot
  id during implementation.
- **Assumption:** AC5 (night re-measurement) is an operational run after
  deploy, mirroring the parent's child `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the plan step may
  decompose it into a follow-on child instead of blocking the code change.
- **Risk:** an endpoint-wide match annotates live work → weakens the truthful
  contract. Mitigation: require no live dispatch record for that slot, and
  cover the negative case with a deterministic test (AC4).
- **Risk:** a slot reported free and immediately reassigned could inherit a
  stale endpoint-wide entry. Mitigation: clear the entry on an observed free
  slot and keep the bounded TTL.
- **Risk (scope creep):** cooldown behaviour (`prefill_thrash_cooldown`) and
  the two anomalous rows (`available_slots=1`, 3.3 s latency) are **out of
  scope** here; record them as `discovered-from` items if confirmed.
- **Risk:** extending `_ABANDON_REASONS` changes the historical baseline
  (247 / 12 poll counts were computed with the narrower set). Mitigation: state
  the change in the report note and in the docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB` — parent: abandoned local dispatches leave
  llama-server busy (completed).
- `LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK` — AC1: abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel
  (completed; this item closes its residual).
- `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037` — AC4: re-measure one comparable night (completed;
  produced the 12-poll baseline).
- `LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2` — regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported
  saturated (completed).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — truthful-status contract (stale capacity hint
  reconciliation) that this item must not weaken.
- `LP-0MVT2KWF0000QTSM` — docs for abandoned-work status and cooldown scope
  (completed).
- Docs: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`,
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`; artifacts under
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is a producer interview needed before drafting, or does the seed context
  suffice?" — Answer (agent, from repo/worklog evidence): the seed context
  states the problem, the measured evidence, the target outcome, six testable
  ACs and the key files; no producer input is required to draft. Source:
  `wl show LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` (description authored by Map), evidence CSV in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent): the parent split re-measurement into its own child
  (`LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`), so the plan step should decompose AC5 the same way.
  **Open to producer override**, not blocking; recorded as an assumption above.
- Q: "Is `measured_cache_deficit` outside the abandonment reasons the
  verification script attributes?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes —
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` `_ABANDON_REASONS` lists only
  `prefill_deadline`, `session_evicted`, `no_progress_watchdog`,
  `client_disconnect`, while `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` exports
  `MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON`. Captured as constraint 5 / AC-relevant scope.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`?" — Answer (OPEN QUESTION, for implementation):
  not determinable from the artifacts alone (no recorded-slot-id field in the
  12-row CSV). Recorded as an assumption to verify with logging, not resolved
  at intake.
### Plan-stage Q&A (added by /skill:plan, session herdr-1793358530-3252013-3553)

- Q: "Is an endpoint-wide (slot-less) registry entry safe, or does it risk
  annotating live work and weakening the truthful contract?" — Answer (agent,
  code evidence + design): safe when the matcher requires that the processing
  slot has **no** lease owner and no live dispatch record; the negative case is
  pinned by a deterministic test before implementation
  (`LP-0MVUVHA55009EU4B`), and `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0 is unchanged in
  intent (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`). Source: `annotate_slots_for_status`
  already computes `owner_session_id`; `_build_slot_to_session_map` provides the
  dispatch-record binding.
- Q: "Should an endpoint-wide entry annotate a slot read from a *stale*
  `/slots` snapshot, and should a stale snapshot clear the entry?" — Answer
  (agent, design decision): annotate yes, clear **no**. The registry entry is
  fresh evidence about an abandonment, while `is_processing=false` is only
  trustworthy from a fresh snapshot; clearing on stale detail would let a
  cached "free" reading drop a live annotation, and the stale path is already
  reconciled by `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- Q: "Which key can represent 'endpoint-wide' without colliding with a real
  slot id?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): an `int` sentinel (`-1`) —
  llama-server slot ids in `/slots` and in `session._slot_owners` are
  non-negative, and the registry dict is typed `tuple[str, int]`, so a string
  sentinel would break the type contract. Recorded as a module constant so the
  assumption is explicit and testable.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show `local_abandoned_slots=0`?"
  — **OPEN QUESTION (carried forward, not resolved at plan time)**: not
  determinable from the 12-row artifact CSV. Routed to implementation child
  `LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK`, which adds `slot_source=` / `abandoned_slot_mismatch`
  diagnostics so the recorded vs observed slot id is answerable from production
  logs; the item's AC requires the answer be recorded (or a follow-on item
  created) before it closes.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent, confirmed at plan time): no — decomposed into follow-on child
  `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, mirroring `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the intake entry
  above remains the authoritative record. **Open to producer override.**

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2** – Regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported saturated (completed)
- **LP-0MRFOF7XO003T7CT** – POST /v1/leases/release — Proxy API endpoint for proactive lease release (completed)
- **LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK** – Abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel on abandonment (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvrmi5hk00558tb, 0mvt2ksn3007qyfk, abandon, abandoned, abandonment (+370 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvrmi5hk00558tb, abandon, abandoned, abort, ac1 (+369 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, 0mvrmi5hk00558tb, abandon, abandoned, abort (+365 more)

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want every queued local wait to record *how it
entered the queue* and *why it left without a slot*, so the abandoned-wait
share can be split by entry path and by cause instead of being a single
opaque 60.7 % — and so a full-budget expiry can never be confused with a
depth-cap refusal.

## Measured need (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Two entry paths feed one queue, and only one of them logs a reason:

| Path | Call site | Abandonments (post-change 24 h) | Logged reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_concurrency_limit` | `provider.py` first `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call | 89 / 314 (28.3 %) | **none** (the fallback line has no `reason=` field there) |
| `local_lease_active` retry | `provider.py` second `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call, after the local dispatch returned a `local_lease_active` 503 | 225 / 314 (71.7 %) | `reason=local_lease_active` |

Per-window split already derivable from the existing `reason=` field (own
measurement, same harness vocabulary):

| Window (24 h) | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | lease-active share | concurrency-limit share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` (pre) | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 41.7 % (20/48) | 23.5 % (4/17) |
| `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` (pre, diurnal) | 136 | 71 | 52.6 % | 53.3 % (57/107) | 50.0 % (14/28) |
| `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` (`52085f09`) | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 61.1 % (225/368) | 59.7 % (89/149) |

Also measured: **all** abandonments are full-budget expiries
(`queued_duration >= 55 s`; 314/314 post-change, 71/71 pre-change diurnal);
depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur, so the 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth`. That distinction is currently *inferred* from
the duration rather than logged.

## Scope

- Log `trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active` on both queue outcomes
  and on the enqueue line, and an explicit `cause=queue_wait_expired|
  queue_depth_exceeded` on both fallback call sites.
- Parse and report the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` in
  `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (the existing harness — do NOT
  create a second report; `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` owns the standalone
  contention-queue residual report).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: add `trigger=` + `cause=` to the two
  `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` and two `contention_queue_dispatch`
  log calls; derive `cause` from the returned action (`elapsed is None` with
  depth at cap → `queue_depth_exceeded`, otherwise `queue_wait_expired`) —
  never guess from the duration in the analyser.
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`: `_KV_TRIGGER`, `_KV_CAUSE`
  regexes; per-band and totals blocks gain `by_trigger` and `by_cause`
  counters; the markdown record renders the split.
- `tests/test_prefill_admission_conversion.py` + proxy tests: synthetic lines
  for both triggers and both causes; a legacy line without the new fields
  degrades to `unknown`, never dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Both fallback call sites log an explicit `cause=` (`queue_wait_expired` vs `queue_depth_exceeded`) and `trigger=` (`concurrency_limit` vs `local_lease_active`); the concurrency-limit site, which currently logs no reason at all, is attributable. Unit-tested from the provider call path.
- AC2: The enqueue line `contention_queue_wait` carries `trigger=` (and keeps `saturation=`), so an enqueue that never resolves is attributable.
- AC3: The harness reports the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` (totals and per band), and a synthetic-line test proves a depth-cap refusal (elapsed ≈ 0, `cause=queue_depth_exceeded`) is distinguished from a budget expiry (`cause=queue_wait_expired`) without inferring from duration.
- AC4: A log line lacking the new fields (pre-change shapes) is parsed as `unknown` and never dropped — asserted by a test using a pre-change line shape.
- AC5: Re-running both committed windows reports the split (expected: 0 depth refusals) with the numbers pasted from tool output, and the record's markdown shows it.
- AC6: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; guardrails `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) / `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) and the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering untouched.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`
- `tests/test_prefill_admission_conversion.py`
- `proxy/tests/` (queue + log-shape tests)

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: the band-attribution fix (own-request join) child.
- `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` — standalone sweep report owner (consumes these fields).
- `LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI` — the completed item that introduced the lease-active queue path.

# Goal

Bring `slots_stale` under **5 %** of `/llama/local/status` polls (the measured target of
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 AC1) by making the `/slots` counts/detail refresh meet its handler budgets
under real load — or, if that is not achievable at the configured budgets, establish the evidence
and move the contract deliberately.

# Problem statement

The 24 h re-measurement of 2026-10-29 (window `2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00` local,
coverage `covered`, no gaps, 2 proxy restarts inside the window at 12:58:34 and 14:09:25) measured:

| Metric | 24 h value | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Status polls | 26,019 | — |
| `slots_stale=true` | **7,698 (29.59 %)** | < 5 % → **missed** |
| stale source | `detail_cache` 7,224 / `counts_cache` 474 / unknown 0 | — |
| stale-poll refresh latency | ≥5 s 2,063 · 2–5 s 3,888 · 1–2 s 1,637 · <1 s 110 | — |
| `capacity_hint` idle/prefill_bound/saturated/abandoned_busy | 16,160 / 6,156 / 3,293 / 410 | — |
| `saturated` with no live local work | 70 (0.27 % of polls) — 65 attributed, 5 unattributable | 0 |
| herdr downtime dispatches (durable trail) | 81 (target ≥ 10) | **met** |
| Local dispatches | 829 (143 sessions, 29 herdr; warm 576 / cold 253) | — |

Same-window trend of the metric on successive builds:

| Window | Build | `slots_stale` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 20:00 → 07:00 (night) | `56a3a28a`/`2d2b6b51` (router `/slots` path) | 79.61 % |
| 2026-10-28 09:30 → 21:30 (12 h) | child-port resolver `f58e8964` live | 53.92 % |
| 2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00 (24 h) | `f58e8964` live + later HEAD | **29.59 %** |

The child-port resolver removed the router from the polling path and roughly halved the stale rate,
but **77 % of the residual stale polls were served from cache after a refresh that took longer than
the 2 s counts / 1.0 s (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) detail budget**. Staleness is therefore no longer a
router artefact: the `/slots` read path still exceeds its budget under load, so `slots_stale` is
reporting real latency, not a truthfulness defect (the cache-time reconciliation of
LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM still holds — only 70 polls, 0.27 %, showed `saturated` without live work).

# Evidence and re-derivation

- Artifacts: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure/` (`measurement.json`,
  `measurement.txt`, `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, `prefill_thrash_skips.csv`,
  `SUMMARY.md`, `provenance.json`).
- Command (read-only, verified tool LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK):

  ```bash
  python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py \
    --since '2026-10-29 01:00' --until '2026-10-30 01:00' --window-closed \
    --label 24h-remeasure --limit 250 --json \
    --write-artifacts ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure
  ```

- Durable herdr dispatch trail re-derived from `wl export` (`author=herdr-downtime` +
  `Auto-dispatched` + `createdAt` inside the window): 81 dispatches, 53 distinct items.

# Not in scope (tracked elsewhere)

- Router `/slots` HTTP 400 responses — LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 (this item is about latency/staleness,
  not 400s).
- Nightly report generator publishing `slots_stale` / `capacity_hint` — LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0.
- Abandoned-dispatch ghosts inflating `abandoned_busy` — LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB.

# Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `/slots` counts/detail read path is profiled under load and the dominant contributor to
  > 2 s refreshes is named with per-path timing evidence (child-port request concurrency, per-poll
  fan-out, llama-server `/slots` cost, or proxy-side serialisation).
- AC2: A 24 h window re-measured with the same tool shows `slots_stale < 5 %` of status polls;
  **or** the item records that the configured budgets cannot be met at peak load, with the measured
  latency distribution, and the producer decides whether to raise the budget or change the target.
- AC3: `capacity_hint=saturated` without live local work stays at 0, or every residual poll is
  attributed (the 24 h run left 5 unattributable out of 26,019).
- AC4: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` reflects the outcome, and the full suite is green.

## Related work

- discovered-from:LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (24 h re-measurement that measured this residual)
- Measurement items: LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ, LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV
- Fix that this residual survives: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (capacity truthfulness, unchanged)

# Plan (plan_complete, 2026-10-31)

Decomposition into three vertical phases, test-first. Effort/risk pre-check returned
`decision=plan` (Medium effort, Medium risk); the plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval=false`, so no approval pause was required.

## Evidence refresh (seed for this plan)

Live window 2026-10-31 00:42 → 04:52 local (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, current HEAD),
read-only analysis:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Status polls | 4,164 |
| `slots_stale=true` | 709 (17.03 %) |
| stale by poll latency | `< 1 s` 11 · `1–2 s` 172 · `2–5 s` 355 · `≥ 5 s` 181 |
| `slot_counts_stale=true` | 0 |
| `slots_detail_stale=true` | 657 |

So the residual is now **entirely the per-slot detail query**, and it is a real latency signal: the
handler awaits `query_llama_status()` (1 s budget) then counts (2 s) then detail
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s) **in series**, and the detail fetch duplicates work the 1 s periodic
refresher already does (`_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at`). Idle child-port
`/slots` costs 0.7–5.5 ms, so the cost is load-dependent backend latency, not route cost.

## Phases and children

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Test: /slots read-path freshness contract (LP-0MVVXGHHB0073W1B) | task | — |
| F1 | Instrument per-phase /slots read-path timings (LP-0MVVXGHT1001I5YX) | task | T1 |
| F2 | Profile 24 h window; name dominant contributor (LP-0MVVXGI490089OX5) | task | F1 |
| F3 | Serve shared /slots snapshot on status path (LP-0MVVXGLTM008ROJ9) | feature | T1, F2 |
| F4 | slots_stale from snapshot age; schema 5 (LP-0MVVXGM54009TOXD) | feature | F3 |
| F5 | Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) | task | F3 |
| F6 | Re-measure 24 h window; record AC2 disposition (LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP) | task | F3, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Docs and full-suite green (LP-0MVVXGN2C004O28B) | docs | F6 |

### Phase A — evidence (T1 → F1 → F2)

Tracer bullet through code → `status_request` log → analysis tool → recorded evidence. Ends with the
dominant contributor named per parent AC1, and an explicit instruction that F3/F4 descriptions are
updated if the evidence contradicts the assumed fix.

### Phase B — fix (T1 → F3 → F4/F5)

Tracer bullet through the handler read path → payload/log → consumer contract → attribution. One
shared `/slots` snapshot; counts and detail derived from the same payload; `slots_stale` defined by
snapshot age rather than cache use; stale reconciliation preserved.

### Phase C — verdict (F6 → F7)

Re-measure a full ≥ 24 h window with the same tool and record either `slots_stale < 5 %` (AC2 first
branch) or the measured latency distribution and the producer decision request (AC2 second branch);
then documentation and full suite (AC4).

## Reused implementations (no new machinery where one exists)

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` — TTL caching + single-flight coalescing (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` — stamped shared snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` — pristine-cache discipline (LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — `slots_stale_attribution.by_source` /
  `by_latency_band`, `--write-artifacts` (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK).
- `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint()` — cache-time reconciliation (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) stays the
  guard that makes snapshot-serving safe.

## Assumptions (documented, not invented requirements)

1. The measured residual is dominated by backend `/slots` latency under load plus per-poll fan-out;
   F2 is the gate that confirms or refutes this before F3 is implemented.
2. A snapshot age of ≤ 2 s (two refresher cycles) is an acceptable freshness budget for a
   dispatcher that polls at ~17 polls/min; the value is env-configurable and revisited in F6.
3. `slots_stale` redefined as age-over-budget is the honest observable; the alternative (keep
   "served from cache") makes the metric unmeasurable once the poll path serves a warm snapshot by
   design. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 in the Appendix, to be confirmed before F4.
4. The item is a `bug` with four ACs, so no epic-level feature splitting below the eight children.

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search slots_stale` / `/slots latency` / `single-flight slots` / `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`: no
completed item covers this scope. Nearest relatives and why they are not duplicates:
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (measurement, closed with a documented miss), LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ (detail-cache
fallback, delivered), LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y (single-flight cancellation, delivered),
LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (post-cancel release lag, different defect), LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (abandoned-work
annotation, delivered).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-31 — initial decomposition: 8 children created (T1, F1–F7), 10 dependency edges wired,
  evidence refresh recorded, AC-section boundary fixed (`# Related work` → `## Related work` so the
  coverage review stops parsing provenance links as acceptance criteria). Stage → `plan_complete`.
